title: Constructing Equations for Shifted Graphs
originalTopic: Graph Shifting: Horizontal and Vertical Translations
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Write a formula for the function obtained by translating the graph of y = x^2 rightward by 3 units and downward by 5 units.

steps.title: Apply Horizontal Translation
steps.explanation: To translate a graph rightward by h = 3 units, replace each occurrence of the input variable x with (x - 3).
steps.why: Horizontal translations replace x with x - h to shift the point of origin rightward.

steps.title: Apply Vertical Translation
steps.explanation: To translate a graph downward by k = 5 units, subtract 5 from the output expression.
steps.why: Vertical translations add or subtract constants from the total function value.

steps.title: Verify Vertex Coordinates
steps.explanation: Evaluating at x = 3 gives y = (3 - 3)^2 - 5 = -5, which matches the expected translation of the parabola's vertex from (0,0) to (3,-5).
steps.why: Feature point verification confirms the translation coordinates.
